We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

actions.marked: **Consult the nearest doctor** if you have breathlessness, giddiness, cough, chest discomfort or pain, or red or watery eyes.

actions.text: On Moderate days, avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor physical exertion.
actions.marked: On Moderate days, **avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor physical exertion**.

actions.text: On Poor days, avoid outdoor physical activities.
actions.marked: On Poor days, **avoid outdoor physical activities**.

athlete.disclaimer: General information from public health guidance, not medical advice.

notes.who: WHO 24-hour guideline levels are set at the 99th percentile, i.e. about 3-4 days a year above the level are expected even where the guideline is met [8].
notes.india: India's 24-hour (and 8-hour) limits must be met 98% of the time in a year; they may be exceeded on 2% of days, but not on two consecutive days [9].
